title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector intervention to support vulnerable communities in drought-affected areas in Bale Zone, Oromia

description.narrative: ltpgtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtIn 2023, the overall humanitarian situation in Ethiopia is remarkably deteriorated. Multiple overlapping humanitarian crises such as ongoing latent conflicts, widespread of violence and climate shocks including prolonged drought and floods, have increased significantly the humanitarian needs. The HRP 2023 targets more than 26 million people in Ethiopia that are in need of humanitarian assistance.ltbrgtClimate shocks, including drought and floods are still threatening the life of vulnerable people and restricted access to basic needs and services in several zones of the country and particularly in the low-land of Oromia and Somali Regions. After the extreme drought, recent rainfall caused flooding in southern and eastern parts of Ethiopia increasing the risk of cholera outbreaks.. The latest flash update on Cholera outbreak (7 may 2023) reported 6,157 cholera cases and 7 million people at high-risk in the regions of Oromia, Somali and SNNP.ltbrgtThe project targets Bale Zone, in Oromia Region and specifically the Gura Damole and Meda Welabu Woredas, due to the huge humanitarian needs caused by the compounded effects of the drought and cholera. For the implementation of the project, COOPI, Imagine1day and MIH have joined forces for delivering a multi sector-integrated response. Specifically, COOPI and MIH, in a division of labor based on expertise, will cover water supply, sanitation, hygiene as well as agriculture, while Imagine1day will work on ensuring that protection needs are addressed, with a particular focus on Gender-Based Violence (GBV). The total targeted beneficiaries for the WASH sector are 18,501 individuals (9,233 female 9268 male) covered by improved access to water sanitation and hygiene promotion, including the distribution of WASH NFIs and water treatment chemicals (6000 individuals M 3016 and F 2984). Related to the Agriculture sector, the Consortium will reach 300 HH (160 female-headed 140 male-headed), through the distribution of agricultural inputs and through restocking intervention finally, 40 Community Animal Health Workers and 6 vet clinics supported through capacity building and health animal treatments input. Under Protection, Imagine1Day will work closely with COOPI's and MIH team to mainstream protection and GBV issues by building capacity of local institutions at community and woreda level 3000 individuals (M 1508 and F 1492) will take part to awareness of on GBV and protection campaign. Finally, 600 case management will be supported through cash or in-kind assistance, as appropriate in order to mitigate the risks of negative coping strategies. ltbrgtFinally, the proposal includes also support through MPCT to be delivered to 300 households this component presented under Agriculture Sector will be coordinated and implemented in collaboration with the Cash Working Group and complementing the sectors WASH, Agriculture and Protection described in the proposal. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
